THE ANOMALY APPEARED DARK-TONED NEAR THE EDGES AND ALSO INCLUDED WHITE AND SILVER SHIMMERY HUES IN THE MIDDLE SECTIONS THAT INDICATED POSSIBLE THICKER OIL. ALSO, THE SLICK DID NOT TEST POSITIVE FOR VEGETATION, AND HAD A STRONG CONTRAST AGAINST THE OCEAN BACKGROUND. IT MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 6 NM IN LENGTH, AND 0.25 NM AT THE WIDEST POINT. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE OUT OF THE NE AT 4 KTS. UNCERTAINTIES: MULTIPLE OIL FACILITIES WERE IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE ANOMALY, AND THEREFORE, A SINGLE SUSPECTED SOURCE WAS NOT CONFIRMED. ADDITIONALLY, THE FULL EXTENT OF THE SLICK WAS NOT DETERMINED DUE TO CLOUD COVER OBSERVED, THAT OBSCURED THE SW SECTIONS OF THE ANOMALY.
